content: I run an online home-goods store with a $72 average order value, a 42% gross margin, and $9 average shipping cost. About 38% of carts are abandoned after shoppers see shipping. I can either offer free shipping above a threshold or run a 15% sitewide discount, but I cannot afford both. Which should I test first, what exact threshold or offer would you use, and how would you measure whether it improved profit rather than just revenue over the next 30 days?

# Test Free Shipping at $85 First

## Why Free Shipping Beats the 15% Discount Here

Run the numbers on contribution per completed order under each scenario:

| Scenario | Revenue | Gross Profit (42%) | Shipping Cost to You | **Net Contribution** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Status quo (customer pays ship) | $72.00 | $30.24 | $0 (customer covers) | **$30.24** |
| Free shipping at $85 threshold | $85.00 | $35.70 | −$9.00 | **$26.70** |
| 15% sitewide discount | $61.20 | $25.70 | $0 (customer still pays ship) | **$25.70** |

The 15% discount *lowers* your contribution per order by $4.54 and does nothing to address the specific friction (sticker shock on shipping). You'd need a **17.7% increase in order volume** just to break even on total contribution — unlikely from a single test.

Free shipping at $85 reduces per-order contribution by only $3.54, but it directly attacks the abandonment trigger *and* pulls AOV upward. The volume recovery from the 38% abandoner pool more than compensates.

---

## Why $85 Specifically

- **Achievable lift:** $13 above current AOV ≈ one additional item for most home-goods baskets. Shoppers will add a candle, a set of towels, a small organizer.
- **Contribution math still works:** Even at $26.70 per order, you need to recover only ~13% of your abandoners to be net-positive on profit (see below).
- **Not so high that it feels out of reach:** $95+ would suppress the recovery effect; $79 barely lifts AOV and erodes more margin.

### Back-of-envelope breakeven

Assume 1,000 cart sessions in 30 days:

- **Today:** 620 complete × $30.24 = **$18,749** contribution
- **With $85 free ship (conservative):**
  - 15% of existing sub-$85 orders lift to $85 (≈74 orders lose $3.54 each → −$262)
  - 20% of existing orders already ≥$85 now get free ship (≈124 orders lose $9 each → −$1,116)
  - Recover 25% of 380 abandoners (95 new orders × $26.70 → +$2,537)
  - **Net change: +$1,159** (~6% profit lift)

Even if you only recover 13% of abandoners, you break even. Anything above that is pure upside.

---

## 30-Day Measurement Plan

### Primary metric: **Net Contribution per Session**

$$\text{Net Contribution per Session} = \frac{\text{Total Gross Profit} - \text{Total Shipping Absorbed}}{\text{Total Cart Sessions}}$$

This single number captures AOV lift, conversion recovery, *and* margin erosion in one figure. If it goes up, the test is profitable — full stop.

### Supporting metrics to diagnose *why*

| Metric | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| Cart abandonment rate (post-shipping step) | Is the friction actually reduced? |
| AOV of completed orders | Are people lifting to $85? |
| % of orders that hit the threshold | Is $85 the right bar, or should it move? |
| Shipping cost absorbed as % of revenue | Margin erosion check |
| Orders per session (conversion rate) | Volume recovery |

### Guardrail metrics (make sure you're not fooling yourself)

- **Revenue alone is not success.** If revenue rises 10% but contribution per session is flat, you're just buying volume with margin.
- **Watch repeat rate.** If the test attracts one-time bargain hunters who never return, 30-day contribution will look fine but LTV suffers. Tag the cohort and check 60-day repurchase.

### Test design

- **If your platform supports it:** Run a true A/B split (50/50 on sessions) for at least 14 days to smooth day-of-week effects. This is far superior to before/after.
- **If you must do before/after:** Use the prior 30 days as baseline, but control for any promotions, email sends, or seasonal shifts. Compare same day-of-week patterns.

### Decision rule at day 30

| Outcome | Action |
|---|---|
| Contribution per session ↑ ≥ 5% | Roll out permanently |
| Contribution per session flat (±3%) | Try threshold at $90; you may need more AOV lift to offset absorption |
| Contribution per session ↓ > 5% | Kill it; the erosion from existing customers outweighs recovery. Test the 15% discount as fallback, but with a minimum-order requirement (e.g., "15% off orders $80+") to protect margin. |

---

## One Tactical Detail

Show a **progress bar or callout** in the cart: *"You're $13 away from free shipping."* The threshold only works if shoppers know it exists and see the gap closing. Without that UX nudge, you'll undercount the AOV-lift effect and may falsely conclude the test failed.
